_comment: Curated recurring ANNUAL events that earn an evergreen page at /{metro}/annual/{slug}/ (kids build only). These pages hold search rank year-round ('<name> 2027' queries start weeks before dates are announced) while dated event pages come and go with the 410 lifecycle. `match` is a case-insensitive regex tested against live event titles to cross-link the current year's event page when it exists. Add entries during weekly prep when a verified one-off is clearly an annual tradition; keep descriptions evergreen (no years, no dates beyond the typical month).

bay-area.title: Hayes Valley Carnival
bay-area.description: A free neighborhood carnival that has run for over a century in Hayes Valley: games and prizes along Hayes Street, food, and a one-ring circus performance on the PROXY stage. One of San Francisco's oldest continuous community traditions.

bay-area.title: Bastille Day SF Festival
bay-area.description: The Bay Area's largest celebration of France's national day: French food, music, petanque games, a waiters' race, and family activities on Embarcadero Plaza, held the weekend closest to July 14.

bay-area.title: Japan Day
bay-area.description: Japantown's summer cultural festival from GenRyu Arts: taiko drumming, awa odori street dance, karate demonstrations, and hands-on origami and calligraphy workshops around the outdoor stage at Post and Laguna.

bay-area.title: Teddy Bear Picnic Day at Fairyland
bay-area.description: Children's Fairyland invites every kid to bring their favorite stuffed animal for a day of rides, storytimes, live shows, and the fluffiest picnic in Oakland — a mid-summer Fairyland tradition.

bay-area.title: Alameda County Fair
bay-area.description: One of the Bay Area's biggest county fairs: carnival rides, livestock barns, horse racing, concerts, and fair food across several weeks at the Pleasanton fairgrounds.

bay-area.title: Nihonmachi Street Fair
bay-area.description: San Francisco Japantown's free community street fair, held the first weekend of August continuously since 1974. Two days of taiko drumming, cultural performances, food booths, and a kids' area celebrate Japanese American heritage across the Japantown blocks.

bay-area.title: Fremont Festival of the Arts
bay-area.description: One of the largest free street festivals in the western United States, run by the Fremont Chamber of Commerce on the first weekend of August: hundreds of artisan booths, a kids' zone with rides and activities, live music stages, and festival food across downtown Fremont.

bay-area.title: Jerry Day
bay-area.description: San Francisco's free annual tribute to Excelsior-born Jerry Garcia at the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater in McLaren Park, held around his August 1 birthday since 2003. An afternoon of live Grateful Dead-inspired music that draws families across the natural grass bowl.

bay-area.title: Watsonville Strawberry Festival
bay-area.description: Watsonville's cherished downtown celebration of the Pajaro Valley strawberry harvest: free admission, carnival rides, a kids' fun zone, live entertainment, and every strawberry treat imaginable, on the first weekend of August.

bay-area.title: Gravenstein Apple Fair
bay-area.description: Sonoma County's beloved harvest fair under the oaks of Ragle Ranch Park in Sebastopol, held every August since 1973 to celebrate the Gravenstein apple: local farms, live music, a children's corral, and apple everything from fritters to fresh press.

bay-area.title: Sonoma County Fair
bay-area.description: The classic August county fair at the Santa Rosa fairgrounds: carnival rides, farm animals and 4-H exhibits, horse racing, nightly entertainment, and the famous flower show. A multi-week Sonoma County tradition for generations of families.

bay-area.title: Gizdich Ranch Apple Picking
bay-area.description: A fourth-generation family ranch in the core of Watsonville's apple country, originally purchased by Croatian immigrant Vincent John Gizdich in 1937. Apple U-Pick, which the ranch calls Pik-Yor-Self, opens in September. The Eata Nita Pie Shop, open since 1980, bakes 16 varieties of pie plus dumplings and puff pastries, and the ranch presses its own award-winning apple juice.

chicago.title: Fiesta del Sol
chicago.description: The largest free Latino festival in the country, filling a mile of Cermak Road in Pilsen with live entertainment, food, carnival rides, and a dedicated children's area every summer for over 50 years.

chicago.title: Chinatown Summer Fair
chicago.description: Chinatown's signature street fair: a lion dance procession, kung fu demonstrations, restaurant samplings, cultural performances, and a children's area along Wentworth Avenue.

chicago.title: Chicago Gospel Music Festival
chicago.description: A free weekend of national gospel headliners and local choirs at the Jay Pritzker Pavilion in Millennium Park — family-friendly and one of the city's longest-running free music festivals.

chicago.title: Chicago Urban League Back To School Festival
chicago.description: The Chicago Urban League's annual Back To School Festival at the James Compton Center in Bronzeville: free food, games, school supplies, and community resources to help families get ready for the school year.

chicago.title: All Seasons Orchard Apple Picking
chicago.description: An orchard in Woodstock where families pick their own among 16,000 apple trees, with Honeycrisp picking as the headliner. The season opens in late August and runs to the start of November, alongside more than 30 barnyard attractions including a petting zoo, pony rides, corn maze, ropes course, mini zip line, sunflower trail, apple cannon, and apple train. Pumpkin picking, apple cider donuts, fresh cider, and caramel apples make it a repeat fall trip.

chicago.title: Kuipers Family Farm Apple Picking
chicago.description: A u-pick apple orchard in Maple Park growing over 45 apple varieties, where each paid admission includes a quarter-peck bag to fill. The picking season runs from late August through the start of November, overlapping the farm's Sunflower Festival and Pumpkin FunFarm. Farmview Railway train rides, the Farmhouse Kitchen, and the Orchard Shop & Bakery keep the rest of the family busy.

seattle.title: Bite of Seattle
seattle.description: Seattle's summer food festival at Seattle Center: hundreds of food vendors, dozens of musical acts, and free admission, running since 1982.

seattle.title: Seafair Torchlight Parade
seattle.description: Seafair's signature evening parade: illuminated floats, marching bands, drill teams, and dragon dancers along the waterfront — a Seattle summer tradition since 1950.

seattle.title: Whidbey Island Fair
seattle.description: A century-old island county fair in Langley: 4-H animal shows, carnival rides, live music, and a small-town Saturday parade.

seattle.title: Seattle Outdoor Theater Festival
seattle.description: A free weekend of outdoor performance in Volunteer Park — a dozen-plus theater companies playing Shakespeare, family shows, and youth workshops across the lawns.

seattle.title: Swans Trail Farms Apple Picking
seattle.description: The u-pick apple orchard at this Snohomish farm holds over 4,000 apple trees and four varieties, including Jonagold and Cosmic Crisp, across five acres. Picking opens in September and the orchard closes for the season on October 31, with a Honeycrisp Apple Festival at the peak. A country store, cidery, and the farm's Fall Festival share the same grounds.

new-york-city.title: Thunderbird American Indian Powwow
new-york-city.description: New York's largest and longest-running powwow: intertribal dance competitions with dancers from dozens of Indian Nations, plus Native art, craft, and food vendors on the Queens Farm meadow.

new-york-city.title: Outhouse Orchards Apple Picking
new-york-city.description: The closest true pick-your-own apple orchard to New York City, in North Salem in northern Westchester County, where visitors hand-pick apples, pears, and peaches from the tree from September into October. Different apple varieties ripen on their own schedule across the season, so what is ready changes week to week. Picking is sold by prepaid bag, either a small 15-pound bag or a large 25-pound bag.

los-angeles.title: Alondra Park Ho'olaule'a
los-angeles.description: California's largest free Hawaiian festival: live hula, island music, traditional food, and cultural booths filling Alondra Park each summer.

los-angeles.title: Nisei Week Japanese Festival
los-angeles.description: Little Tokyo's nine-day celebration of Japanese American culture each mid-August, running since 1934. The Grand Parade and the closing Plaza Festival are the two big free family anchors, alongside taiko, dance, exhibits, and food throughout the district.

los-angeles.title: Los Rios Rancho Apple Picking
los-angeles.description: Apple picking at this Oak Glen ranch runs from Labor Day weekend through Thanksgiving weekend, with early picking sometimes starting in August. Many of the apple trees are more than 80 years old; apples are sold by the pound and baskets and picking implements are provided. The rest of the property fills a full day with a petting zoo and miniature farm, tractor rides, a corn maze, pumpkin picking, nature trails, horse-drawn wagon tours, and live music on weekends.

los-angeles.title: Riley's Farm Apple Picking
los-angeles.description: A working apple orchard and living history farm in Oak Glen with pick-your-own fruit, where apples come in from September through the end of harvest. Riley's grows over 30 varieties and specializes in heirloom apples, ones bred for flavor rather than shelf life. Costumed living history adventures covering the Revolutionary War, Civil War, Gold Rush, and colonial farm life run alongside the picking.

boston.title: Puerto Rican Festival of Massachusetts
boston.description: A multi-day celebration of Puerto Rican culture in Franklin Park: live performances, traditional food, carnival rides, and family activities, drawing tens of thousands each summer.

boston.title: Revere Beach International Sand Sculpting Festival
boston.description: The East Coast's largest sand sculpting festival: world-class sculptors compete on America's first public beach, with a kids' zone, food vendors, and evening fireworks.

boston.title: Minuteman Library Crawl
boston.description: A week-long summer scavenger hunt across the Minuteman Library Network: pick up a free passport at any participating library, then visit libraries across Greater Boston on their featured crawl days, find each library's hidden clue, and collect stamps. Completed passports enter a grand-prize drawing. Around two dozen libraries take part, from Arlington and Watertown to Natick, Needham and Newton — a free, all-ages tradition that turns library-hopping into a family road trip.

boston.title: Honey Pot Hill Orchards Apple Picking
boston.description: A Stow orchard that is typically open for apple picking from early August into early November, with pick-your-own apples straight off the tree. Hayrides run for a small per-person charge for anyone over age three, donuts are made fresh daily, and the farm store carries produce and baked goods. The farm also books field trips, group outings, and birthday parties, making it a standing early-fall outing for Boston-area families.

boston.title: Shelburne Farm Apple Picking
boston.description: A pick-your-own apple farm in Stow, about 20 miles west of Boston, that reopens for the picking season in August. Beyond the orchard rows there are hay rides, farm animals to visit, John Deere tractor and Gator playgrounds, and a Great Pumpkin bounce house. Warm cider donuts and live music round out a classic New England fall farm visit.

atlanta.title: Atlanta Ice Cream & Wellness Festival
atlanta.description: A free summer Saturday in Piedmont Park combining ice cream vendors with family fitness: live music, yoga and Zumba sessions, wellness screenings, and children's activities.

atlanta.title: B.J. Reece Orchards Apple Picking
atlanta.description: A family orchard in Ellijay, about an hour north of Atlanta in the North Georgia mountains, where U-Pick apples run through September and October. As the farm puts it, for many visitors this is a tradition that spans generations. Alongside picking there is a petting zoo and other farm activities, plus a market and bakery known for fried apple pies and apple cider donuts.

atlanta.title: Hillcrest Orchards Apple Picking
atlanta.description: A self-described family friendly orchard in Ellijay offering U-Pick apples during the fall season, with weekday farm activities continuing after picking ends. The farm has a petting zoo, orchard tours, food, and photo spots throughout the property. It sits in the same North Georgia apple belt as Ellijay's other generational orchards.

austin.title: Zilker Summer Musical
austin.match: zilker summer musical|singin' in the rain
austin.description: Austin's free outdoor summer musical tradition since 1959: a full Broadway-style production on the Zilker Hillside Theater lawn, Thursday through Sunday nights all summer. Bring a blanket and picnic.

austin.title: Brick Rodeo
austin.description: The Texas LEGO fan convention: hundreds of custom builds and displays from fan builders, with public exhibition days for families.

houston.title: Mayor's Back 2 School & Health Fair
houston.match: back 2 school (?:&|and) health fair|mayor's back 2 school
houston.description: The City of Houston's annual back-to-school fair at the George R. Brown Convention Center, held every early August since 2011: 20,000 free backpacks with school supplies plus on-site dental, vision, and health screenings for Houston-area elementary students. Registration required; families ride METRO free to the event.

philadelphia.title: Linvilla Orchards Apple Picking
philadelphia.description: Linvilla grows more than 25 apple varieties across 20 acres of orchards in Media, about 30 minutes south of Philadelphia. Apple picking starts in early August with the earliest varieties and runs through the fall as later varieties ripen into November. The farm pairs picking with hayrides, barnyard animals, a playground, fishing, train rides, and pony rides, so the orchard trip doubles as a full day out.

washington-dc.title: Larriland Farm Apple Picking
washington-dc.description: Larriland Farm has been owned and operated by the Moore family since 1973, growing over 20 crops and 90-plus varieties on a pick-your-own farm open from late May into mid-November. Apples ripen late August through October with many varieties available, and a field ticket is required to pick. The Red Barn farm market needs no ticket, and a Fall Festival caps the apple season.

washington-dc.title: Prince William County Fair
washington-dc.description: Virginia's largest county fair, held in Manassas every summer for 75 years: nine days of midway rides, demolition derbies and grandstand shows, livestock exhibitions, and fair food. General admission includes all grandstand and midway events.

san-diego.title: Volcan Valley Apple Farm Apple Picking
san-diego.description: Julian's u-pick apple farm spreads 7,000-plus trellis-grown trees and seven apple varieties across 10 scenic acres, picking from late August through mid-October as weather and crop permit. The trellis system keeps fruit low and reachable for pickers of every age and height, from toddlers just learning to walk to grandparents who prefer to keep their feet on the ground. Wide rows between the trees make it stroller and family friendly.

honolulu.title: Duke Kahanamoku OceanFest
honolulu.description: Waikiki's multi-day celebration of Duke Kahanamoku, held each August around his birthday: ocean sports across surfing, paddling, and swimming, a keiki surf festival, the opening ceremony at Kuhio Beach, and the birthday lei draping at the Duke statue. Many shoreline events are free to watch.
